content.heading: Epistolary jurisdiction
content.text: The Supreme Court or a High Court may, in appropriate cases, treat a letter, telegram, or similar informal communication addressed to the Court or a Judge as a writ petition under Article 32 or Article 226 where the communication discloses a serious allegation of violation of fundamental or other legal rights of persons who cannot themselves approach the Court. Conversion of correspondence into a proceeding is discretionary and subject to verification of genuineness and public interest. Epistolary practice does not create a new writ; it is an access device within existing writ jurisdiction. Anonymous, vague, or privately motivated communications are liable to be rejected.
